abstract: The long-term durability of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) remains a critical hurdle for their widespread commercialization, largely because of chemical degradation of the membrane electrode assembly (MEA) by unintentionally generated free radicals during operation. Defective ceria (CeO2-x) nanoparticles have emerged as promising radical-scavenging additives through reversible Ce3+/Ce4+ redox cycling. However, their radical scavenging efficiency is limited by the sluggish regeneration of surface Ce3+ species, which are the active species for radical scavenging, leading to a gradual loss of their initial scavenging capability during long-term cell operation. Here, we report a strategy to accelerate Ce3+ regeneration kinetics by maximizing heterointerface-derived interactions through simple seed-mediated growth of defective ceria on the surface of a metal-organic framework (MOF). In particular, UiO-66-NH2 undergoes partial amorphization and dissolution during the CeO2-x nanoparticle growth, which enables intimate interfacial contact and enhanced electronic coupling with CeO2-x. The resulting UiO-66-NH2/CeO2-x heterostructure exhibits improved redox cycling and higher Ce3+ retention under oxidative conditions than commercial ceria nanoparticles. Moreover, when incorporated into the cathode catalyst layer of the MEA, the UiO-66-NH2/CeO2-x significantly suppressed the performance degradation, enabling stable single-cell operation for over 500 h under an accelerated durability test.
